mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (ضبحا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), like «أصبح ماؤكم غورا».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (قدحا): a pure maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)], because (فالموريات) means «فالقادحات» (those that strike sparks). [Translator's note: the bracketed gloss is added for clarity.]

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (صبحا): an adverb of time, governed by (المغيرات).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (نقعا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), made accusative by (أثرن).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (إذا بعثر): the governing word (ʿāmil) in (إذا), according to al-Mubarrad, is (بعثر). Neither (يعلم) nor (خبير) governs it, because knowledge and taking heed are not what is required of man at that time; one takes heed only in this world. And as for (يعلم): what comes after (إنّ) does not govern what precedes it. [Translator's note: the source text here reads «ويعلم ولا يعمل ما بعد إن فيما قبلها», which is somewhat disjointed; it has been rendered according to its evident sense.] Were you to say «يوم الجمعة إن زيدا قائم», it would not be permissible except as two separate utterances, with an ʿāmil implied for (يوم), as though you said «اذكر يوم الجمعة» (remember Friday) and then said «إن زيدا قائم»; and (قائم) can in no way govern it. As for the second (يومئذ), the governing word in it is (خبير). It is permissible for what comes after the lām to govern what precedes it [Translator's note: the printed text has «ابعد اللام», read as «ما بعد اللام»], because the lām is, in the implied structure, meant to be at the mubtadaʾ (subject); it entered the khabar (predicate) only because (إنّ) entered upon the mubtadaʾ. So the khabar governs what precedes it, even though it contains a lām, according to the original rule of the lām, which in the implied structure is before the mubtadaʾ.
